releases.notes:
CC-Aeroworks 1.5.0 completes the one-way TeutonLib integration and expands stationary and moving control desks.

Highlights:

- Migrates peripheral lifecycle, computer workspaces, channel groups, named wire signals, hosted computers, Sable geometry, bounded network sessions and Simulated docking access to public TeutonLib 1.5.0 APIs.
- Preserves saved computer IDs, labels, files, channel UUIDs, group bindings, item components and public Lua APIs.
- Adds persistent UUID-based desk assemblies with Create-style placement, separation, bridging and a 64-segment limit.
- Integrates Create Contraption Controls and Train Controls as native desk/stand row segments.
- Adds a default-enabled mobile contraption runtime, embedded computer persistence, moving terminal access and a public mobile peripheral adapter API.
- Splits programmable displays into normal/advanced small/large variants with persistent colour control and advanced-computer touch support.
- Replaces separate Radar Display items with optional Create: Radars sources for advanced displays.
- Uses TeutonLib visible-world Sable geometry for wireless modems and GPS-backed information sources.

Verification completed against Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.234, CC:Tweaked 1.120.2, Sable 2.0.5 and TeutonLib 1.5.0: clean build and unit tests, all 26 GameTests, dedicated-server smoke, static Python/Lua/bytecode contracts, architecture checks and the real client workspace matrix.

releases.notes:
## Changes

- Admins can choose global display density or individual resolutions per display slot. `display.useGlobalResolution` defaults to `true`, preserving the global `display.ppb` setting.
- With global resolution disabled, Lua programs can call `desk.setDisplayResolution(socket, ppb)` or `display.setResolution(event, ppb)`. Values range from 16 to `display.maxIndividualPpb` (default 256; configurable up to 1024). The result contains `width`, `height` and `ppb`.
- Individual resolutions persist and synchronize to clients. Changing density clears the pixel raster; setting the same density preserves pixels. Dismounting a display resets its slot setting.
- Both small and large displays support touch and draw with an **advanced computer in the active console network**. A normal or absent computer disables touch, including events sent to external peripherals. Script bindings survive computer replacement.
- Pixel operations, module descriptions and hit geometry use the effective slot resolution. Running gestures are discarded after resolution or computer changes. Radar displays retain their resolution logic.

## Required dependencies

Minecraft 1.21.1 and NeoForge 21.1.234 or newer. **TeutonLib 1.2.2 is required on both client and server** (supported range: >=1.2.2, <1.3.0). Install [TeutonLib v1.2.2](https://github.com/TeutonStudio/TeutonLib/releases/tag/v1.2.2) separately.

## Verification

- Build and all 101 unit tests pass.
- All 12 GameTests pass, including independent display slots, real NBT persistence, rotated hit geometry, computer tiers and external touch-event delivery.
- Both Lua tests and all 31 repository and bytecode checks pass.
- Isolated dedicated server reaches Done; isolated client initializes resources and rendering with TeutonLib 1.2.2.
- Interactive pointer/draw checks, moving Sable-world rendering and multiplayer reconnect tests remain outstanding. The client reports third-party Create: Radars model/resource warnings.

See [release verification](https://github.com/TeutonStudio/CC-Aeroworks/blob/v1.4.2/docs/test-results/release-1.4.2.md).

## Artifacts

- `cc-aeroworks-1.4.2.jar`
- `cc-aeroworks-1.4.2.jar.sha256`

releases.notes:
## Highlights

- Normal Aeroworks control desks now share a computer inventory slot across their row. Insert or extract a normal or advanced CC:Tweaked computer from the module overview, including shift-click support.
- Existing computer desks migrate automatically when loaded; legacy items migrate when placed. The combined-block recipe is retired.
- Breaking the host transfers its computer to the larger remaining piece, preferring left on a tie. The last desk drops the computer separately. Computer ID, files, label, terminal size, capacity, wire channels and channel groups are preserved. Joining occupied rows retains an advanced computer first and ejects extras with their data.
- Normal control modules can bind Lua scripts in their settings and run them on input changes, including releases and signed axis values. See [control scripts](https://github.com/TeutonStudio/CC-Aeroworks/blob/v1.4.0/docs/control-scripts.md).
- Channels includes a coordinate and target-face editor alongside the Cable workflow, with loading/removal of existing targets and cable consumption checks.
- Fixed channel cycling restoring the first channel when clicking a target after scrolling.

## Compatibility

Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.228; dependency requirements are unchanged from 1.3.4. Existing computer desks are migrated to ordinary consoles with a shared computer slot.

## Verification

- 95 unit tests, all 11 GameTests, all 31 repository verification scripts and the Lua control-script tests pass.
- The isolated dedicated server reaches the startup `Done` marker without a known fatal marker.
- Interactive client visual checks and manual multiplayer GUI checks remain outstanding.

See [release verification](https://github.com/TeutonStudio/CC-Aeroworks/blob/v1.4.0/docs/test-results/release-1.4.0.md) for completed automated checks and remaining manual checks.

## Artifacts

- `cc-aeroworks-1.4.0.jar`
- `cc-aeroworks-1.4.0.jar.sha256`

releases.notes:
## Highlights

- Radar and display diagnostics are disabled by default, even when global DEBUG logging is enabled.
- Independent `debug.radar` and `debug.display` server-config switches enable diagnostics at INFO without additional logger settings. Connected clients use the server settings.
- Disabled radar diagnostics skip trace counters, throttling updates and expensive diagnostic message creation. Genuine warnings, errors and startup messages remain available.
- Fixes radar source selection on Sable ships using projected interaction distances. Ownership and reach checks remain enforced by the server.
- Radar source lists show live connection status and server-confirmed selections. Inactive radar displays explain missing links, missing radar assignments and stale data.
- Restores the lower item-slot border beneath category rows in the Aeroworks creative tab.

## Radar setup

The native Create: Radars network needs both a Controller → Radar assignment and a Controller → Display endpoint assignment. Placing a controller next to a radar does not assign it automatically. Use the Data Link item to select the controller, then link the radar; separately link the display desk. Other displays in the same CC-Aeroworks desk multiblock can select that linked ingress without their own Data Link.

## Optional diagnostics

Both defaults are `false` in `cc_aeroworks-server.toml`:

```toml
[debug]
radar = false
display = false
```

NeoForge creates the server config under `config/`; an existing `<world>/serverconfig/cc_aeroworks-server.toml` takes precedence as a world override. See [configuration](https://github.com/TeutonStudio/CC-Aeroworks/blob/v1.3.4/docs/configuration.md).

## Compatibility and verification

Minecraft 1.21.1; dependency requirements are unchanged from 1.3.3. No world-data migration is required.

- 88 automated tests and all 31 repository verification scripts pass.
- Dedicated-server startup passes with and without Create: Radars.
- An isolated world-copy client test confirms native rendering for both radar display sizes, shared-source synchronization, Sable source selection and rejection outside player reach.
- Interactive visual checks and a dedicated server with a connected graphics client remain outside the completed checks. Full details: [release verification](https://github.com/TeutonStudio/CC-Aeroworks/blob/v1.3.4/docs/test-results/release-1.3.4.md).
